blog_posts.title: State of the Workbench
blog_posts.content: Decided to separate my general thoughts from my specific hardware builds. This feed will just be my day-to-day nonsense, rants, and updates. The desk is currently a disaster zone but we are making progress.

blog_posts.title: Letting the Magic Smoke Out
blog_posts.content: Note to self: 12V and 5V rails are not interchangeable just because the jumper wires are both red. Blew the voltage regulator on the new synth board entirely off the PCB.

projects.title: Cyberdeck_V1
projects.desc: Heavy-duty, field-ready portable compute terminal built from rugged components.

logs.title: Why do we still use Phillips screws?
logs.content: I just stripped three screws trying to open this vintage 90s chassis. Torx exists. Hex exists. Why did humanity settle on a screw head specifically designed to cam out and ruin your day?

logs.title: Sourcing the Chassis
logs.content: Found an old industrial telecom testing unit at the surplus yard. It's built like a tank. Ripping out the guts today to see if I can fit a Raspberry Pi 5.

projects.title: Eurorack-Mutilator
projects.desc: Custom step-sequencer Eurorack module focused on rough logic switching.

logs.title: Desk is officially a hazard
logs.content: Current desk inventory: 4 half-finished microcontrollers, a soldering iron I forgot to turn off, and a massive pile of loose resistors.

logs.title: Schematic Drafting Phase
logs.content: Sketching the logic gates on scratch paper. I want this module to sound actively broken, introducing intentional clock jitter at high rates.

projects.title: The_Iron_Vault

logs.title: Configuring the SAS Controller
logs.content: Finally got the LSI HBA card flashed to IT mode. FreeNAS is recognizing all 6 drives natively now. True storage peace of mind achieved.
